One can verify that the global KL condition fails to hold for the inner maximization problem of \eqref{example} at any $x\in [1,2]$.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own conventions, for x in \Omega\setminus dom p one has \partial p(x)=\emptyset, hence \partial\Psi(x)=\emptyset and dist(0,\partial\Psi(x))=\infty, so the level set in (Lev_set) becomes \cL(x)={y:0<F^*(x)-F(x,y)<\infty}, i.e., all non-optimal y. Since Assumption 1(iii) is quantified over any open \Omega\supset\cX=dom p, it demands the GLOBAL KL inequality in y at every x outside dom p. For the Example, at y=\pi (and nearby) one has \nabla_y\phi(x,\pi)=-x\sin\pi=0 while \phi^*(x)-\phi(x,\pi)=x(\sqrt2/2+1)>0, so the KL inequality fails for every x>0; any open \Omega\supset[1,2] contains such x outside [1,2]. The source verifies the KL property only on a bounded level set and only for x\in[1,2], so the Example cannot satisfy Assumption 1 as written, contradicting the remark and the advertised breadth of the 'local' KL class whenever dom p\neq\mathbb{R}^n.

failure_location.quote: For example, the minimax problem in Example~\eqref{example} satisfies the local KL condition but not the global one.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the level set so its radius stays finite off dom p, e.g. \cL(x):={y:0<F^*(x)-F(x,y)\le\gamma\min\{\dist(0,\partial\Psi(x)),1\}^\sigma\}, and restrict Theorem thm:Phi_smooth to \epsilon\le 1 (the only regime used downstream); with a suitable \gamma the Example then satisfies the assumption (its verified KL region covers the capped level set), and all proofs and complexity bounds go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's motivating example is not covered by the central assumption it is meant to illustrate, and for every problem with dom p\neq\mathbb{R}^n the 'local' KL hypothesis still includes the global KL condition in y at infeasible points. The theorem statements remain logically valid, but they are established for a strictly narrower class than the paper advertises.
issues.title: Local KL assumption still imposes global KL off dom p, so the motivating Example does not satisfy Assumption 1
issues.why_classification: The supported repair edits the paper's central local-KL definition and clips Theorem 1's \epsilon-range (the alternative of quantifying only over \cX breaks the a.e.-to-everywhere differentiability extension at boundary or lower-dimensional dom p). No new proof architecture is needed and every complexity guarantee survives, so the loss is limited, but the fix is more than a local or degenerate-case edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the proximal operators of $p$ and $q$ can be computed exactly
the number of evaluations of the proximal operator $p$ equals the number of iterations

issues.failure_explanation: Each outer iteration minimizes a linear-plus-quadratic-plus-p objective over the ball \cB(x^k,r); this is the proximal operator of p+\mathcal{I}_{\cB(x^k,r)}, not of p. Assumption 1(ii) only posits exact computability of the prox of p, and for general closed convex p the constrained prox cannot be obtained exactly from finitely many prox-p calls (the natural 1-D dual root-finding is only convergent), while the analysis uses exactness of the argmin (the strong-convexity comparison in (argmin_constrained) and the optimality condition (xhatk-opt)). Even the paper's own numerical example, p(x)=0.01\|x\|_1+\mathcal{I}_{\cB(0,1)}(x), has no closed-form exact solution of this step. Hence Theorem thm:operations' claim that the number of evaluations of the proximal operator of p equals the number of iterations (at most \widehat{K}_\epsilon) does not follow from the stated oracle.

failure_location.quote: x^{k+1} = \mathop{\arg\min}_{x \in \cB(x^k, r)} \Big\{ \langle \nabla_x f(x^{k}, y^{k}), x \rangle + \frac{L_k}{2} \|x - x^k\|^2 + p(x) \Big\}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption 1(ii) to require exact computation of the ball-constrained composite proximal operator (prox of p plus a ball indicator), or restrict p to classes where this is available in closed form; alternatively, propagate a controlled inexactness of the outer subproblem solve through Lemmas lem:subsolver_output and lem:gen_converge. With the strengthened oracle every stated bound is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The iteration complexity of Theorem thm:outer_bound is unaffected as a statement about the idealized iteration, but the algorithm is not implementable under the stated oracle (exact prox of p only), and the first-order oracle accounting for p in Theorem thm:operations is unsupported; the advertised applicability to simple p with exactly computable prox is narrowed.
issues.title: Outer ball-constrained subproblem is not an evaluation of the prox of p assumed available, so the prox-p oracle count is unsupported
issues.why_classification: A supported repair is a limited strengthening of the oracle assumption (one the paper's own numerical example meets only approximately) or a contained but nontrivial inexactness analysis; no new global proof architecture is required and all rates survive, but the fix goes beyond a local or degenerate-case edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Additionally, notice that $\partial F^*$ and $\partial p$ are outer semicontinuous on $\cX$. Hence, $\partial \Psi$ is outer semicontinuous on $\cX$, which together with $x^k \to x$, $s^k \in \partial \Psi(x^k)$, and $s^k \to s$ implies that $s \in \partial \Psi(x)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition \partial^\infty F^*=\{0\} (local Lipschitzness of F^*) yields only the inclusion \partial\Psi\subseteq\partial F^*+\partial p via the standard sum rule (Clarke/Rockafellar-Wets); equality of Clarke subdifferentials additionally requires subdifferential regularity of F^*, which the paper nowhere establishes and which can fail in general (e.g., for F^*+p=-|\cdot|+|\cdot| one has \partial_C F^*(0)+\partial p(0)=[-2,2]\neq\{0\}=\partial_C(F^*+p)(0) while \partial^\infty F^*(0)=\{0\}). The equality is load-bearing: from s^k\in\partial\Psi(x^k) and outer semicontinuity of the summands the proof obtains s\in\partial F^*(x)+\partial p(x), and concluding s\in\partial\Psi(x) uses exactly the unjustified reverse inclusion.

failure_location.quote: By this and $\Psi=F^*+p$, one has $\partial \Psi=\partial F^*+\partial p$ on $\cX$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality step by the standard closedness argument for the limiting/Clarke subdifferential of the lsc function \Psi: bounded s^k\in\partial\Psi(x^k) with x^k\to x imply, via the valid inclusion \partial\Psi\subseteq\partial F^*+\partial p and local boundedness of \partial F^*, that x\in dom p and \Psi(x^k)\to\Psi(x); outer semicontinuity of \partial\Psi along function-value-convergent sequences then gives s\in\partial\Psi(x). No statement changes.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 6's proof is incomplete, so the openness of \cU_\epsilon used in Theorem thm:Phi_smooth (and transitively in Lemmas lem:subsolver_output and lem:gen_converge and Theorems thm:outer_bound and thm:operations) lacks justification as written. The statement of Lemma 6 is nonetheless correct and standard.
issues.title: Lemma 6 (openness of U_epsilon) uses Clarke sum-rule equality justified only by horizon subdifferential vanishing
issues.why_classification: Only one proof step is unjustified; the lemma's conclusion is true and is restored by a routine, standard argument with no change to any statement, rate, or scope, so all dependent results stand once the local step is patched.
